title: wt sync --json
description: What a rebase onto trunk would do to every worktree of a repository, as `wt sync --json` prints it on stdout: one overview object, or with --all, --roots or --profile an array of them, one per repository. It fetches trunk and each worktree branch's own remote (unless --no-fetch) and writes nothing else. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

ownRemote.description: Since 1.3.0: a branch against its own remote, the remote-tracking ref a push of it would replace: <branch>@{push} when git resolves it, else refs/remotes/origin/<branch>. Never the upstream as such: a branch cut from trunk often tracks trunk and pushes to its own name. See docs/json.md.

ref.description: The remote-tracking ref, as remote/branch (origin/feat/x); null only when no ref could be named: for none, and for unknown unless it is a ref that could not be compared.

state.description: none: nothing to check: the ref is trunk's, or does not exist. gone: the branch names a ref the remote no longer has. unknown: where a push lands cannot be read from a tracking ref (a mirror remote, several push URLs, a push URL that is another repository than the fetch URL), or the branches or the remotes cannot be read at all, or the two tips cannot be compared; a run goes on unchecked. inSync: the same commit. ahead: only the branch has commits of its own. behind: only the remote has; a run fast-forwards the branch first. rebased: both have, and the remote's are old versions of the branch's (its tip is a tip the branch once had, or every commit only it has is matched patch for patch); a run goes on. diverged: both have, otherwise; a run refuses unless --allow-diverged.

commit.description: The remote commit compared with; null for none, gone and unknown.

ahead.description: Commits only the branch has; null for none, gone and unknown.

behind.description: Commits only the remote has; null for none, gone and unknown.

fetched.description: true: the remote side is from this command's fetch. false: as last fetched (--no-fetch, trunk's fetch or this branch's own failed, or a remote whose fetch refspec is not the standard one).

blocks.description: Why a run would refuse for it; non-null only when a run would. diverged with state diverged, for a branch a run would rebase: --allow-diverged goes on. operation, dirty, session with state behind: it cannot be fast-forwarded, because a git operation is in progress there, the checkout has tracked changes, or an agent session is busy in it.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows.

repo.description: The main checkout, as wt sweep --json names the repository.

name.description: The repository's name: its main checkout's directory name.

trunkSource.description: How trunk was determined, first match wins, from local refs alone (since 1.1.0): config — MAIN_BRANCH in the wt configuration file; originHead — refs/remotes/origin/HEAD; conventional — the first of development, main, master that exists locally or on origin (since 1.1.1; before, main, master, trunk, development, develop, ranked by where each exists); currentBranchGuess — no longer produced since 1.1.1: when nothing names trunk, detection fails and the repository reports noConfiguration. Null when trunk is.

trunkRef.description: origin/<trunk>, what every worktree is assessed against.

onto.description: The trunk commit assessed against; null when trunk is not known here.

fetchError.description: The fetch failed: the overview is against trunk as last fetched.

declared.description: Trunk declares .wt-sync.yaml. Without it the worktrees are assessed but a run rebases none.

token.description: Names what a run would start on; pass it to wt sync rebase --expect or wt sync --rebase --expect. Since 1.3.0 a worktree refused only for having diverged from its own remote is in it too, with the remote commit, for a run under --allow-diverged. Null when a run would start on nothing.

error.description: Why there is no overview: trunk not known, the repository not readable.

sessionsError.description: Agent sessions could not be listed; sessions are then empty, not known empty.

worktrees.description: Every worktree but the main checkout, in git's order.

group.description: The overview's group. current is on trunk already, which the human overview leaves out. Since 1.3.0 a worktree whose class is current or stale only at its remote's commit, which a run fast-forwards it to, is ready.

class.description: What the simulated rebase found; unknown when the assessment failed (error).

verified.description: false is the overview's question mark (recipe?): a script owns a path and the replay could not be carried past it.

verdict.description: What wt sync rebase <work> would do: start on it, skip it, or refuse it untouched.

runnable.description: wt sync --rebase, with nothing named, takes it.

reason.description: Why it is not runnable; null when it is.

handedOver.description: An earlier run left a conflict here for a person: wt sync resume or wt sync undo.

planFile.description: The plan file of a handover.

kind.description: Since 1.2.0 also codex: a Codex session.

stack.description: Every worktree a run on this one would move, parents first; just this one without a stack; empty when detached.

stops.description: Every stop the simulated rebase reached, in order.

strategies.description: The declared strategies that resolved a file at some stop, each once.

deferredDeclared.description: Since 1.4.0. The deferred steps .wt-sync.yaml declares on the trunk commit in onto, in the declared order: what a run goes through once it has rebased this worktree, itself or through wt sync resume after a handover. Declared, not predicted: each may run. A step with no paths does, after every finished rebase; one with paths only when the rebase changed one of them; none after a step that failed. The same list on every worktree, also one a run would skip or refuse, where nothing is rebased and so none runs: verdict says which. Empty when trunk declares none or has no .wt-sync.yaml.

ownRemote.description: Since 1.3.0. A worktree a run would refuse for it has verdict refuse, runnable false and the reason in words; its group is needsYou, or skipped when a busy session is in it, whatever blocks says; class stays about trunk. For a branch that is behind and will be fast-forwarded, class, behind, ahead and stops are those of the remote commit: what the run rebases. When that class is current or stale there is nothing to rebase: the row is verdict proceed, runnable true, group ready, and a run fast-forwards the branch and is done.

declaredStep.description: One deferred step .wt-sync.yaml on trunk declares under defer:, before any rebase. See docs/json.md.

step.description: Its run line: the string deferred[].step carries for it in wt sync rebase --json.

paths.description: The globs that gate it, as declared. Empty: it runs after every finished rebase. Otherwise it runs only when the rebase changed a path one of them matches, which is not known before the rebase.

resolved.description: Every conflicted file here was resolved by a strategy.

yours.description: The first stop no strategy resolves: a run hands it to a person.

strategy.description: The strategy that claims it; null when none does.

note.description: Why a strategy refused it, or what a lift did.
